# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 10 LORNA VANE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“I’m going for a walk to the outside shore tonight,” Nell said to Gog and Magog one evening in October. Because Hugh had crossed the harbor, there was nobody else for her to inform. Her small domain was in the spotless organization to be anticipated of anyone raised by Thirza Abernethy, and Nell believed she might head toward the shore with a unburdened mind. Her excursions to the shore had been numerous and wonderful, at times alongside Hugh, at times alongside Captain Saul, and at times by herself with her own reflections and fresh, keenly-sweet dreams that were starting to bridge existence with their rainbows. She cherished the mild, vaporous harbor shore as well as the silvery, wind-frequented sand shore, yet she cherished the rock shore most of all, with its precipices and caverns and heaps of wave-eroded boulders, along with its coves where the pebbles gleamed beneath the pools; and it was toward this shore that she traveled tonight.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0000 }

A three-day autumnal tempest of rain and gale-force winds had passed. The breakers had smashed against the rocks with a deafening sound, the pale foam and spray had swept wildly across the bar, and the previously tranquil blue waters of Seven Gulls Harbor had become agitated, hazy, and battered by the storm. Now that the weather had cleared, the coastline appeared thoroughly cleansed by the gale; the air was completely still, yet an impressive swell persisted, crashing against the rocks and sand in a magnificent froth of white—the sole motion amid the vast, all-encompassing quiet and serenity.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0001 }

“Oh, this is a moment worth living through weeks of storm and stress for,” Nell exclaimed, joyfully casting her distant look over the churning waves from the summit of the precipice where she was standing. Soon she climbed down the sharp incline toward the small bay beneath, where she appeared enclosed by stone, ocean, and firmament.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0002 }

“I intend to perform a dance and a song,” she stated. “No person exists in this place to observe me—the seagulls will not report news about it. My behavior can be as wild as I desire.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0003 }

Gathering up her skirt, she twirled past the firm band of sand right beyond the arrival of the waves, whose exhausted froth nearly touched her feet. Spinning repeatedly while laughing in the manner of a child, she arrived at the small promontory extending east from the cove; thereupon she halted abruptly, turning bright red; she lacked privacy; a spectator had observed her dancing and laughing.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0004 }

Perched upon a rock on the promontory, partially concealed by an overhanging crag, sat the young woman possessing golden hair and eyes the color of the ocean. Her gaze was fixed directly upon Nell, displaying a peculiar countenance that combined astonishment, compassion, and—could that truly be?—jealousy. Wearing no hat, her magnificent tresses, resembling Browning’s “gorgeous snake” to an even greater degree, were secured around her brow by a scarlet band. She was attired in a dark-colored gown of extremely simple design; nevertheless, wrapped around her midsection, accentuating its beautiful lines, was a bright sash of red silk. Though her hands, locked above her knee, were tanned and slightly roughened by labor, the flesh of her neck and face remained cream-white. A swift ray of the setting sun pierced a low cloud in the west, illuminating her locks. In that instant, she appeared to embody the soul of the ocean itself—encompassing its every enigma, its full intensity, and its entire fleeting fascination.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0005 }

“You—you must think me crazy,” stammered Nell, attempting to regain her composure. It was really too bad to be caught by this regal girl indulging in such a childish outburst—she, Mrs. Dr. Carrow, who had all of a married woman's poise to maintain!
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0006 }

“No,” the girl replied, “I do not.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0007 }

She uttered no further words; her tone lacked any emotion; her demeanour was somewhat off-putting; nevertheless, an expression in her eyes—at once keen and hesitant, rebellious and beseeching—prevented Nell from carrying out her intention to leave. Rather than departing, she took a seat on the rock next to the girl.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0008 }

“Let us state our names,” she remarked, using the grin that had always succeeded in gaining trust and goodwill. “My name is Mrs. Carrow—and my home is that small white dwelling further along the harbor coast.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0009 }

“Indeed, I am aware,” the girl stated. “My name is Lorna Vane—Mrs. Rufus Vane,” she appended in a formal tone.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0010 }

Absolute astonishment kept Nell quiet briefly. That the girl had a husband had never crossed her mind—she appeared to possess no spousal traits whatsoever. Furthermore, that she was the exact neighbor Nell had envisioned as an ordinary Seven Gulls homemaker! Nell struggled to rapidly shift her perspective to accommodate this incredible transformation.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0011 }

“So—so the gray house farther up the stream is where you reside,” she faltered.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0012 }

“Indeed. My visit to you ought to have been paid a considerable time back,” the second speaker remarked. No justification or apology for her failure to do so was tendered by her.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0013 }

“It is my desire that you WOULD pay a visit,” uttered Nell, regaining a degree of composure. “Our proximity as neighbors dictates that friendship should exist between us. The singular defect of Seven Gulls lies in that very aspect—the neighbors are slightly too few in number. In all other respects, it embodies perfection.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0014 }

“Is it to your liking?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0015 }

“LIKE it! I adore it. It is the loveliest location I have ever seen.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0016 }

“I have not visited many locations,” Lorna Vane uttered, unhurriedly, “however, I have constantly believed that this place was extremely beautiful. I—I adore it, as well.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0017 }

Her speech matched her appearance, being delivered with a mixture of timidity and enthusiasm. It struck Nell curiously that this unusual girl—she could not help thinking of her as a “girl”—was capable of revealing much more if she wished.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0018 }

“I frequently visit the coast,” she continued.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0019 }

“I agree,” Nell remarked. “We should have crossed paths in this place prior to now.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0020 }

“It is likely that your visits occur at an earlier hour in the evening than mine. My arrivals are usually late—nearly dark. Furthermore, my favorite time to arrive is right after a storm—resembling this one. The ocean pleases me less when it is still and serene. What I enjoy is the struggle—along with the crash—and the noise.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0021 }

“In every one of its states, I adore it,” Nell stated. “What Linger Lane represented back home is what the ocean at Seven Gulls means to me. It appeared so unchained—so fierce—this evening that my own spirit untethered itself as well in harmony. For that reason, I leaped beside the water in such an untamed manner. Naturally, I never imagined that a single soul was watching. Had Miss Winifred Tolley caught sight of me, she’d have predicted a bleak future ahead for the unfortunate young Dr. Carrow.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0022 }

“Do you know Miss Winifred?” Lorna asked, chuckling. Her laugh was exquisite; it surfaced all at once and unpredictably, possessing much of the delightful charm found in a baby’s. Nell joined in the laughter, as well.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0023 }

“Oh, yes. On multiple occasions, she has come down to my house of dreams.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0024 }

“The residence you dream of?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0025 }

“Ah, Hugh and I use that beloved, silly small moniker for our residence. We merely utilize it when it is just the two of us. It escaped my lips before I realized.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0026 }

“Thus the small white home belonging to Miss Russell is THE home of your dreams,” Lorna stated in amazement. “A home of dreams was once mine—however, it was a palace,” she inserted, laughing in a way whose sweetness was spoiled by a slight tone of mockery.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0027 }

“Oh, I formerly had dreams about a palace, as well,” Nell remarked. “I imagine every girl does. And afterwards we establish ourselves happily in houses with eight rooms that appear to satisfy every wish of our hearts—for the reason that our prince is present. YOU ought to have truly possessed your palace, however—you possess such beauty. You MUST permit me to speak it—it simply must be spoken—I am almost exploding with awe. You are the most beautiful creature I have ever beheld, Mrs. Vane.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0028 }

“You must address me as Lorna if we are to be friends,” the other declared with a strange passion.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0029 }

“Certainly I shall. Furthermore, I am called Nell by MY companions.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0030 }

“I guess my appearance is lovely,” Lorna continued, staring fiercely toward the ocean. “My loveliness is something I despise. My desire is that I had perpetually been as dark-skinned and ordinary as the darkest-skinned and most ordinary female in that fishing village across the way. So, how do you regard Miss Winifred?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0031 }

The sudden shift in topic precluded any additional disclosures.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0032 }

“Isn’t Miss Winifred a darling?” Nell asked. “Last week, Hugh and I had an invitation to her home for a state tea. You know the phrase about groaning tables.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0033 }

“I think I remember coming across that phrase in newspaper write-ups about weddings,” Lorna said, with a smile.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0034 }

“Indeed, Miss Winifred gave a groan—or, to be exact, a creak—without a doubt. It was beyond belief that she would prepare such a quantity of food for just two average folks. In my opinion, she possessed every sort of pie imaginable—save for lemon pie. According to her, she won the award for lemon pies at the Port Marlow Exhibition a decade prior and refrained from baking them ever since to avoid risking her standing for them.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0035 }

“Did you manage to consume a sufficient amount of pie to satisfy her?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0036 }

“I was not. Hugh captured her affections through eating—I will not reveal the exact amount. Her statement was that she had never met a man who failed to prefer pie over his Bible. Are you aware that I adore Miss Winifred?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0037 }

“I do as well,” Lorna remarked. “In all the world, she is my closest friend.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0038 }

Nell silently pondered why Miss Winifred had never brought up Mrs. Rufus Vane to her if that was the case. Miss Winifred had undoubtedly spoken openly regarding all the other people living in or around Seven Gulls.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0039 }

“Is that not lovely?” Lorna inquired, following a short hush, as she indicated the stunning sight of a ray of sunshine streaming through a fissure in the cliff behind them, spanning a murky emerald basin at its bottom. “Were I to arrive at this spot—and witness only that single view—I should return satisfied.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0040 }

“The impacts of shadow and light right along these coasts are marvelous,” concurred Nell. “The harbor is visible from my small sewing room, and I perch by its window to satisfy my vision. Never during two consecutive minutes are the shadows and hues identical.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0041 }

“And you don't ever feel lonely?” Lorna inquired suddenly. “Not ever—when nobody else is with you?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0042 }

“No. I do not believe I have ever experienced true loneliness in my life,” Nell replied. “Even during times when I am by myself, I enjoy wonderful company—dreams, imaginations, and pretendings. I ENJOY being by myself occasionally, merely to reflect on things and TASTE them. However, I adore friendship—along with pleasant, cheerful little moments with others. Oh, WILL you not come visit me—frequently? Please. I think,” Nell added, laughing, “that you would care for me if you were acquainted with me.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0043 }

“I ponder whether YOU might find ME agreeable,” Lorna stated in earnest. A compliment was not what she was seeking. Her gaze swept over the sea, where crests of foam illuminated by the moon were starting to form like garlands, and darkness gathered within her eyes.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0044 }

“I’m sure I would,” Nell said. “And please don’t consider me completely irresponsible simply because you caught me dancing on the beach as the sun was setting. I will undoubtedly become dignified eventually. You see, I haven’t been a wife for very long. I still feel like a girl, and occasionally even a child.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0045 }

“My marriage has lasted for twelve years,” Lorna remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0046 }

This was yet one more thing that was impossible to believe.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0047 }

“Well, your age cannot possibly match mine!” cried Nell. “When your marriage took place, you had to be a mere youngster.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0048 }

“Sixteen was my age,” Lorna said, standing up and gathering the cap and jacket that were next to her. “My age is twenty-eight today. Well, returning is something I must do.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0049 }

“I have to go as well. It is likely that Hugh is at home now. However, I am extremely happy that the two of us visited the beach this evening and ran into one another.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0050 }

Lorna remained silent, which made Nell feel somewhat discouraged. Although she had extended a candid offer of amity, it was received with little grace, even if it had not been entirely rejected. Without speaking, they ascended the cliffs and traversed a pasture where the moonlight turned the soft, pale wild grasses into what resembled a creamy velvet rug. Upon arriving at the shore lane, Lorna turned around.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0051 }

“This is my direction, Mrs. Carrow. You will visit me on occasion, will you not?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0052 }

It seemed to Nell that the invitation had been flung in her direction. Lorna Vane appeared to offer it with hesitation, in her view.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0053 }

“I will attend if it is truly your desire,” she stated with a slight chilliness.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0054 }

“Oh, I do—I do,” cried Lorna, her intensity breaking out as though it had shattered a limitation placed upon it.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0055 }

“I will join you, in that case. Good-night—Lorna.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0056 }

“Have a good night, Mrs. Carrow.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0057 }

Lost in deep thought, Nell made her way back to the house and recounted her story to Hugh.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0058 }

“Therefore, Mrs. Rufus Vane does not belong to the people who recognize Joseph?” Hugh asked in a playful manner.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0059 }

“No—o—o, not precisely. Even so—it seems to me she WAS among their number at one time, though she has left or been forced into exile,” Nell remarked thoughtfully. “She undeniably differs greatly from the local women. One cannot converse regarding eggs and butter with HER. To imagine that I had been conceiving of her as another Mrs. Agatha Sowerby! Did you ever catch sight of Rufus Vane, Hugh?”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0060 }

“No. While I have noticed a few individuals laboring in the farm's fields, I am unsure which one was Vane.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0061 }

“He was never spoken of by her. I am CERTAIN that happiness eludes her.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0062 }

“Based on what you are telling me, I imagine she got married prior to being mature enough to understand her own mind or feelings, only to discover when it was too late that she had erred. It happens to be a quite frequent tragedy, Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0063 }

“A woman of quality would have managed the situation as well as possible. It is obvious that Mrs. Vane allowed it to fill her with bitterness and resentment.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0064 }

“Let us withhold judgment until we are certain,” begged Nell. “Her situation is not so typical, I believe. Once you encounter her, Hugh, her allure will make sense to you. It exists completely distinct from her looks. My impression is that her personality is abundant, one a companion could step into like a realm; however, owing to some cause, she excludes everybody and locks her potential inside, preventing it from growing and flowering. Well, I have tried hard to describe her to myself from the moment I departed from her, and I have come as close as possible to doing so. Miss Winifred is the person I intend to question regarding her.”
{: #nw-v04-c10-p0065 }
